summary: H1 is identified as the root cause with high confidence (0.82): payment-service's outbound mTLS client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) expired at exactly 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, causing 100% of bank-partner-api calls to fail at the TLS handshake while the HTTP error-rate dashboard stayed green (~0.22%). The failures are deferred as PENDING_RETRY on an async outbound rail, so no HTTP 5xx was generated — 311 in-window ERRORs, bank_api_error_rate 0.21%→100%, payment_success_rate 99.4%→~2.5%, restarts flat at 0, all flipping in the same 12:15:00Z bucket and first error logged at 12:15:27Z. Every change-based alternative is excluded by mechanism and path: no deploy or config change falls in the symptom window, and the only relevant config change (cfg-2502, timeout 3000→5000ms at 11:20Z) cannot cause a TLS handshake rejection and precedes onset by ~55 minutes. The one residual uncertainty is H1 vs H2 (bank-side TLS/CA change), which is permanently unobservable because bank-partner-api has has_telemetry=false; the untruncated log text explicitly names OUR client cert and its notAfter matching the onset to the second, so the payer-side origin is established and H2 remains only an unfalsifiable fallback.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Client mTLS certificate on the bank rail expired at 12:15Z (our side), failing 100% of outbound bank calls while HTTP error-rate stays green
ranked_hypotheses.statement: payment-service's outbound mTLS client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) had notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z. At that exact instant every outbound call to bank-partner-api began failing at the TLS handshake (alert 45, expired certificate), so transfers were marked PENDING_RETRY (async/deferred) rather than returning 5xx. Because the failure is on a non-HTTP dependency path handled asynchronously, the payment-service HTTP error-rate panel stayed flat (0.16-0.28%) while payment_success_rate collapsed from 99.4% to ~2.5% and bank_api_error_rate went to 100%. No deployment, config change or cert-rotation event sits near the onset; the expiry is a certificate lifecycle event invisible to change tooling.
ranked_hypotheses.root_cause_service: payment-service (outbound bank mTLS client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal)

causal_chain.claim: payment-service's client certificate for bank-partner-api reaches notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z

At 12:15Z the TLS handshake to bank-partner-api is rejected ('tls: expired certificate (alert 45)'); first error log 12:15:27Z, identical CN/notAfter signature repeating 80+ times through 12:59Z (sustained, unchanging)

The rejection is specifically a certificate expiry — no other TLS alert code (42/48) appears anywhere in the window — and the peer-reported 'remote error' prefix denotes where alert 45 was surfaced, not that the peer's cert expired

The identical expired-certificate signature is absent from every other component swept in 12:10-13:00Z (kafka, api-gateway, settlement-service, ledger-db, auth-service, order-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine — 8 components, 0 matches), localizing the event to payment-service's bank-rail cert
bank_api_error_rate flips to a sustained 100.0% for every bucket 12:15-13:55 and payment_success_rate collapses to ~2.5%
Payment attempts fail fast and are deferred as PENDING_RETRY rather than crashing the request path; p99 latency drops 320ms->140ms, restarts stay 0
Because the failure is on an async/deferred dependency path outside the HTTP handler's error accounting, the synchronous HTTP error_rate panel remains green — the reported dashboard discrepancy
No deploy/flag/cert-rotation event correlates with the 12:15Z onset, consistent with an automatic certificate lifetime expiry invisible to change tooling

assumptions: The notAfter value is taken from log text (the only cert evidence exposed; no cert inventory/secret store exists in the toolset — F19/F20/F21/F38).
payment-service's view of the handshake is authoritative: bank-partner-api has has_telemetry=false, so the peer's own certificate/CA state can never be directly observed (F6, F16, F37).
PENDING_RETRY deferral is what suppresses HTTP 5xx; supported by 140 PENDING_RETRY lines and restarts=0 but with no queue/worker metric (F5, F24, F27).
The 8 swept services are representative of the wider fleet; ~6 known_services remain unqueried (budget), so fleet-wide confinement is not proven (F33, F34).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bank/PSP side degraded or changed its TLS/CA configuration, rejecting our (still-valid) client certs
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The vendor side of bank-partner-api altered its TLS/CA trust (cert rotation, CA change, or an outage) at 12:15Z, causing our otherwise-valid client certificate to be rejected at the mTLS handshake. From payment-service's view this is indistinguishable from our own cert expiring, because bank-partner-api has no telemetry and all evidence is payer-side. This matches the reporter's suspicion of a bank-side fault and category dependency_failure.

causal_chain.claim: bank-partner-api changes/degrades its TLS termination or CA trust at 12:15Z
mTLS handshake from payment-service is rejected, surfacing as 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' in payment-service logs
bank_api_error_rate reaches 100% and payment_success_rate falls to ~2.5%
Failures are deferred (PENDING_RETRY) so the HTTP error-rate panel stays green

assumptions: Bank-side telemetry is permanently unavailable (has_telemetry=false; bank-partner-api change/deploy records are count 0 — F37), so this cannot be directly excluded; its survival rests only on that unobservability.
A peer-side CA/trust change would coincidentally produce alert 45 and the exact same notAfter instant as our cert lifetime.

ranked_hypotheses.title: cfg-2502 timeout relaxation to 5000ms masked/destabilized the bank rail
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 11:20Z config change raising bank.api.timeout_ms from 3000 to 5000 on the failing dependency edge perturbed the bank integration and contributed to the transfer failures.

causal_chain.claim: Altered timeout behavior destabilizes the bank rail
Bank calls begin failing, cascading to payment failures at 12:15Z

assumptions: A timeout increase could plausibly cause failures.
The change effect was delayed ~55 minutes.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Wrong mechanism and wrong timing: a 3s->5s timeout relaxation would mask slowdowns, not produce a hard 100% TLS handshake rejection (F14). The change precedes onset by ~55 minutes with no mechanism linking it to a TLS handshake (F15), and the actual error is a certificate expiry (alert 45), which no timeout value can cause (F4, F28).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared component (ledger-db / kafka) or settlement-service dep-5510 indirectly poisons payment-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A failure in a shared component (ledger-db, kafka) or the settlement-service deploy dep-5510 (new CSV exporter, sharing ledger-db and kafka) degraded the payment path, with metrics spread across services.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5510 (settlement-service v1.9.0, new CSV exporter) deploys at 10:30Z
Shared-component degradation propagates to payment-service outbound failures

assumptions: Settlement-service actually stresses shared resources enough to affect payment-service.
A db/queue failure could manifest as a bank-side TLS handshake failure.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: dep-5510 is not on the payment-service call path (F17) and shares only ledger-db/kafka, whereas the observed failure is specifically on the external bank rail (F2, F16) with a TLS certificate signature (F4, F25). kafka logs show zero cert/TLS-alert matches (F31), and no mechanism connects a db/queue issue to 'tls: expired certificate'. Timing is also poor (deploy 10:30Z vs onset 12:15Z).

facts.statement: payment-service HTTP 5xx error_rate stayed flat and low across the whole window (mean 0.22%, all 12:15-13:55 buckets 0.16-0.28%), confirming the dashboard was genuinely green and did not reflect the incident.
bank_api_error_rate flipped to a sustained 100.0% in the 12:15:00Z bucket (from ~0.21% at 12:00-12:10) and stayed at 100% through 13:55.
payment_success_rate collapsed in the same 12:15:00Z bucket from ~99.4% to ~2.5% (range 2.0-2.77 through 13:55), i.e. ~97.5% of payments failing while HTTP error_rate looked normal.
First error signature at 12:15:27Z: 'payment 45f233b6 marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected'; 311 ERRORs matched in-window (cert failure x171, mTLS PENDING_RETRY x140).
bank-partner-api is an external dependency with has_telemetry=false and no direct telemetry; it can only be observed through payment-service, its only caller.
Across all services, the window 2026-04-02T11:30:00Z-13:59:00Z contains 0 deployments and 0 config changes.

The only change on the failing dependency edge is cfg-2502: payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms changed 3000→5000 at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z by p.nair — a timeout relaxation, which would mask slowdowns rather than cause a 100% TLS handshake failure.
Neither change sits inside the reported symptom window 11:30Z-13:59Z; the closest change (cfg-2502 at 11:20Z) precedes the 12:15:00Z onset by ~55 minutes, so no change correlates with onset.

The only deployment on 2026-04-01/02 before the incident is dep-5510 (settlement-service v1.9.0 'new CSV exporter', 2026-04-02T10:30:00Z, not rolled back); settlement-service is not on the payment-service call path per the dependency map.

payment-service dependency map: outgoing edges to ledger-db (db, shared), bank-partner-api (external, vendor, has_telemetry=false) and kafka (queue-produce, shared); incoming api-gateway -> payment-service (http). The failed edge is the external bank rail.

No cert/secret inventory or cert-manager exists in the toolset: config-store queries over 2026-03-01→2026-04-02T13:59Z return only cfg-2502 and zero records referencing a certificate, secret, CN, notAfter or rotation; dependency lookups for 'cert-manager' and 'secret-store' fail with unknown service.

No certificate rotation or renewal event exists in change/deploy records: over 2026-03-20→2026-04-02T13:59Z across all services there is exactly one config change (cfg-2502) and one deployment (dep-5510), neither cert-related, and nothing timestamped near the 12:15:00Z rotation window.

The untruncated error text explicitly attributes the expiry to OUR side: 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' — the named expired certificate is the payment-service client (mTLS) cert, with notAfter coinciding exactly with the metric/error onset bucket.

The 'remote error' prefix denotes where the alert was surfaced (reported by the handshake peer bank-partner-api), not that the peer's own certificate expired — the same message names our client cert as the expired one.
The expired-certificate signature is sustained, not transient: it repeats 80 times between 12:16:44Z and 12:59:53Z with identical text, same CN and same notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z.
No TLS alert code other than 45 appears: 'alert 48' over 12:00-13:59Z and 'alert 42' over 12:10-13:00Z both returned total_matched 0 in payment-service.

8 of the non-payment components show 0 in-window hits for cert/TLS-alert terms (kafka for 4 patterns; auth-service, order-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine for 'certificate'; plus api-gateway, settlement-service and ledger-db), while payment-service is the only component with matches (134 TLS-related ERRORs from 12:15:27Z).

Historical precedent for the mechanism exists but is a lead only: HIST-106 'Settlement mTLS certificate expired' (2025-06-30, settlement-service, root cause 'Client certificate expired; no renewal automation', category credential_expiry); no prior orangeinvest.internal fleet/CA renewal batch event is recorded.

The external peer bank-partner-api is entirely outside the change-record system: config-change and deployment queries scoped to it return count 0, so no bank-side TLS/CA reconfiguration can be observed — this makes bank-side origins unverifiable from records, not false.

assumptions: The notAfter value (2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) is taken from payment-service runtime log text; there is no cert inventory, secret store or cert-manager in the toolset (F19-F22, F38), so the certificate's metadata cannot be independently confirmed.

payment-service's view of the handshake is treated as authoritative, since bank-partner-api has has_telemetry=false and the peer's own certificate/CA state can never be directly observed (F6, F16, F37).

PENDING_RETRY deferral on the async outbound rail is what suppresses HTTP 5xx; this is supported by 140 PENDING_RETRY lines and restarts=0, but no queue/worker metric was available to confirm the deferral mechanics (F5, F24, F27).
The 8 swept services are treated as representative of a broader fleet; ~6-8 known_services were never queried (budget), so fleet-wide confinement of the cert expiry is not proven (F33, F34).
Change/deploy record sparsity reflects genuine absence of changes rather than API truncation; a change made before 2026-04-01 or hidden by API sparsity could have been missed (F7, F13).

Alert 45 being side-agnostic means the payer-side log text is the only discriminator between our client cert expiring (H1) and a bank-side CA/TLS change (H2); this inference rests on log text alone (F26, F30).

timeline.event: Only pre-incident deployment in the period: dep-5510, settlement-service v1.9.0 'new CSV exporter' (not on the payment-service call path; not rolled back).

Config change cfg-2502 by p.nair raises payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms from 3000 to 5000ms ('Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory') — a relaxation on the bank rail edge, ~55 min before onset.

Certificate lifecycle event: payment-service mTLS client cert (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) reaches notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z. In the same bucket, bank_api_error_rate flips to 100% and payment_success_rate collapses to ~2.5%, while HTTP error_rate stays low (0.16-0.28%).
First error log: 'payment 45f233b6 marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' — failures begin being deferred rather than returned as 5xx.

Paired root-cause error text: 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z'.
Support lead reports INC-005 [SEV-2]: ~40 tickets about failed fund transfers in the last 15 minutes, while the payment-service error-rate panel looks normal.
The identical expired-certificate signature repeats 80 times (same CN, same notAfter), alongside 54 PENDING_RETRY entries — a sustained, unchanging cert-expiry condition.
End of window: bank_api_error_rate still 100%, payment_success_rate still ~2.0-2.77%, HTTP error_rate still 0.16-0.28%, restarts 0; no cert-related change or deploy exists to explain or remediate it.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately renew/replace the expired outbound bank-rail mTLS client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal (obtain a new cert from the issuing CA/partner onboarding channel and load it into payment-service's bank-rail TLS client configuration, then roll/restart the payment-service instances that hold it), then flush/replay the accumulated PENDING_RETRY transfers to bank-partner-api.
recommended_actions.rationale: The cert notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z coincides exactly with the onset bucket and the error text names this client cert as expired (F4, F24, F25, F27); renewal restores the handshake and drained retries restore the ~97.5% of failed payments (F2, F3, F5).

recommended_actions.action: Alert the on-call incident commander to open a vendor channel with bank-partner-api to confirm that no TLS/CA trust change occurred on their side at ~12:15Z, and to confirm they observed alert 45 for our client cert specifically.
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 (bank-side CA/TLS change) is permanently unobservable from our toolset (bank-partner-api has_telemetry=false; config/deploy records return count 0; tc-016 failed not_found), so peer confirmation is the only way to close the H1-vs-H2 separation and the reporter's bank-side suspicion (F6, F16, F37).

recommended_actions.action: Do not roll back cfg-2502 (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000→5000ms) as a mitigation; it is not causal.
recommended_actions.rationale: A timeout relaxation cannot cause a hard TLS handshake rejection and it precedes onset by ~55 minutes with no linking mechanism (F8, F14, F15); reverting it would add risk without addressing the handshake failure.

recommended_actions.action: Verify recovery after renewal with explicit checks: bank_api_error_rate returns to ~0.2%, payment_success_rate returns to ~99.4%, and the 'expired certificate' / PENDING_RETRY log signatures stop appearing.
recommended_actions.rationale: These are the exact metrics and log signatures that moved at onset (F1-F4), so they are the definitive verification signals for closure and for confirming the retry backlog has drained.

recommended_actions.action: Add a dashboard/alert on bank_api_error_rate and payment_success_rate (and on dependency-edge success for non-HTTP/external rails) so a non-HTTP rail failure cannot hide behind a green HTTP error-rate panel.
recommended_actions.rationale: The incident was invisible to the HTTP error-rate panel because failures were deferred as PENDING_RETRY on an async outbound rail while error_rate stayed at 0.16-0.28% (F1, F5, F24).

recommended_actions.action: Introduce certificate expiry inventory and automated renewal (cert-manager or equivalent) for client certificates, with expiry warning alerts at least 30/14/7 days out, and register the bank-rail client cert as a managed component with its CN and notAfter.
recommended_actions.rationale: No cert/secret inventory, cert-manager or vault node exists in the toolset, and no rotation/renewal event exists in change records, so this expiry was invisible to both monitoring and change tooling (F19-F22, F35, F36, F38); the same mechanism caused prior incident HIST-106 ('Client certificate expired; no renewal automation') (F18, F23).

recommended_actions.action: Add a startup/readiness check and a periodic self-test in payment-service that performs a live mTLS handshake to bank-partner-api and fails health (or alerts) if the client certificate is expired or within N days of expiry.
recommended_actions.rationale: The payment-service process never restarted and kept failing silently at the handshake while restarts stayed at 0 (F5), so without an active handshake self-test the expiry can persist undetected (F4, F24, F27).

recommended_actions.action: Complete the fleet-wide cert/TLS sweep over the unqueried services (market-data-service, notification-service, exchange-gateway, user-db, redis-cache, exchange-api, kyc-provider, email-provider) to confirm the expiry is confined to this single client identity.
recommended_actions.rationale: Only 8 of many components were verified clean (F33, F34, F29); the remaining ~6-8 services were never queried due to budget, so confinement to payment-service is not proven fleet-wide.

data_gaps: No cert/secret inventory exists in the toolset (no secret store, cert-manager or vault; config store has zero cert/CN/notAfter records), so the certificate's notAfter and any renewal history can only come from payment-service runtime log text, not from an authoritative certificate store (F19-F22, F38).

bank-partner-api is an external node with has_telemetry=false and no edges; its metrics, logs and change/deploy records are unavailable (count 0), so the bank side cannot be directly inspected and H1 vs H2 cannot be separated from peer-side telemetry (F6, F16, F37, tc-016 failed not_found).

No per-endpoint, per-pod or per-region breakdown was obtainable — payment-service's available metrics are aggregate only — so it cannot be confirmed whether 100% of transfers failed vs other payment types, or whether one pod/region was spared.

No 4xx-vs-5xx breakdown and no timeout/queue/worker metrics exist in the available metric set, so the PENDING_RETRY deferral mechanism suppressing 5xx is inferred from log counts and restarts=0 rather than measured from a queue metric (F5, F24).

No structured log field dump (pod, node, cert serial, handshake peer address, TLS version, request-id) was retrievable, and no log-context query (±10-20 surrounding lines) was executed, so peer attribution rests solely on the in-message 'remote error' prefix (F26).

Change/deploy APIs returned empty for the tight 11:30Z-13:59Z window and only one item each when broadened to 2026-04-01T00:00Z; whether the APIs are truncated or genuinely sparse is unverified, and pre-2026-04-01 changes were not visible, so the absence of further changes is not proven (F7, F13).

No historical incident documents the exact 'green error-rate dashboard during payment failures' / async-silent-failure pattern; only category-level analogues (HIST-106, HIST-105, HIST-114) were retrieved, so there is no direct precedent confirming the silent-failure pattern (F11, F39).

The client-cert identity search over 2026-03-01→2026-04-02T13:59Z could only be performed as a metadata search (config changes, deployments, dependency graphs, historical incidents) because no full-text record search endpoint was available; cert-identity mentions outside these four record types are unchecked (F35, F39).
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Authoritative evidence from bank-partner-api's side (metrics, logs or a vendor statement) that the bank rotated its TLS trust bundle or CA configuration at ~12:15Z, rejecting otherwise-valid client certs — this would move H2 above H1.

A certificate inventory or CA record showing a second live certificate with notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z shared across multiple services (a fleet/CA renewal batch), which would show this is not an isolated single-client expiry and shift the conclusion toward a broader credential-management failure (F40).
Successful handshake and restored payment_success_rate after a bank-side change alone, without renewing our client cert — this would demonstrate the failure was peer-side and falsify H1.

Discovery of a cert rotation, secret change or renewal deploy record near 12:15Z that was hidden by API truncation or falls outside the queried record window, which would introduce a change-driven cause currently excluded (F7, F13, F15).

Evidence from the unchecked services (market-data-service, notification-service, exchange-gateway, user-db, redis-cache, exchange-api, kyc-provider, email-provider) showing the same expired-certificate/alert-45 signature, which would indicate a shared/CA-side event rather than a payment-service-local cert expiry (F29, F33, F34).

Structured log fields or a log-context dump showing that the expired certificate named in the error is the peer's (bank-partner-api) rather than our own client cert, which would overturn the payer-side attribution that carries H1 (F25, F26, F30).

dep-5510 (settlement-service, 10:30Z) is not on the payment-service call path per the dependency map, so even though it is not rolled back it cannot directly explain payment-service's outbound bank-rail failure.

findings.statement: No cert/secret inventory is exposed by the available toolset: querying the config/feature-flag store for payment-service over 2026-03-01→2026-04-02T13:59Z returns exactly one record (cfg-2502, key 'bank.api.timeout_ms', 3000→5000 at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z) and zero records referencing any certificate, secret, CN, notAfter or rotation key.

There is no secret-store or cert-manager component to query: resolving the dependency graph for service 'cert-manager' and for 'secret-store' both fail with unknown service, and the enumerated known_services list (api-gateway, auth-service, order-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service, payment-service, settlement-service, notification-service, exchange-gateway, ledger-db, user-db, redis-cache, kafka, exchange-api, bank-partner-api, kyc-provider, email-provider) contains no certificate/secret inventory service.

The payment-service dependency graph (depth 3, both directions) exposes no secret store, vault, cert-manager or keystore node — only api-gateway (http inbound), ledger-db (db), bank-partner-api (external), kafka (queue-produce) — so the client certificate used for the bank rail is not represented as a managed/observed component.

No certificate rotation or renewal event exists in the change/deploy records: over 2026-03-20→2026-04-02T13:59Z across ALL services there is exactly one config change (cfg-2502) and exactly one deployment (dep-5510, settlement-service v1.9.0, 2026-04-02T10:30:00Z); neither is a cert/secret rotation and nothing is timestamped near the 12:15:00Z rotation window.

Historical cert-inventory precedent is a lead only: HIST-106 'Settlement mTLS certificate expired' (2025-06-30, settlement-service, symptoms 'tls handshake failures','expired certificate', root_cause 'Client certificate expired; no renewal automation', category credential_expiry) matches the failure mechanism, but past incidents are leads and not evidence about the current incident.

The full ERROR log entries around the onset in payment-service (12:15:27Z–12:17:57Z, 7 entries, untruncated) contain two distinct signatures: 6x 'payment <id> marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' (ids 45f233b6 at 12:15:27Z, 7b4c31a9, 62f775af, 7ccfdb22, aca0ea9d, 03ba104b) and exactly 1x the paired error 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' at 12:16:44Z. No additional fields/labels beyond ts, level, message are present in the returned entries.

refs.quote: bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z

findings.statement: The error text explicitly attributes the expiry to OUR side: it names 'our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z'. The certificate identified as expired is the payment-service client (mTLS) certificate, and its notAfter (2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) coincides exactly with the metric/error onset bucket.

The same message does carry a peer-attribution field: the fragment 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' frames the alert as reported by the remote handshake peer (bank-partner-api), while simultaneously naming our client cert as the expired one — so the 'remote error' prefix denotes where the alert was surfaced, not that the peer's own certificate expired.

The expired-certificate signature is not a one-off: it repeats 80 times in payment-service between 12:16:44Z and 12:59:53Z (identical text, same CN and same notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z), alongside 54 PENDING_RETRY entries, in a result that was truncated (134 matched, 40 returned) — so the 12:16:44Z entry is the first of a sustained, unchanging cert-expiry signature, not a transient.

refs.quote: "pattern":"bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert <n>); our client cert CN=payments-","count":80,"first_seen":"2026-04-02T12:16:44Z"

findings.statement: No TLS alert code other than 45 appears: a payment-service search for 'alert 48' over 12:00–13:59Z returned total_matched 0, and a search for 'alert 42' over 12:10–13:00Z also returned total_matched 0.

The identical 'expired certificate' text was NOT found in the other services I could query for 12:10–13:00Z: api-gateway, settlement-service and ledger-db each returned total_matched 0, while payment-service returned 134 TLS-related ERRORs from 12:15:27Z onward. This is evidence against a broadly shared CA-side event, but it covers only 3 of the other services in the window.

Interpretation for H1 vs H2: the log wording ('our client cert ... notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z') points at our own client certificate having expired at the onset instant, rather than a peer/CA reconfiguration by the bank; the 'remote error' prefix only says the peer reported alert 45. This is inference from log text alone — no peer-side telemetry exists to confirm the bank's view.

kafka shows no trace of the expired-cert signature in 12:10-13:00Z: searches for 'expired certificate', 'alert 45', 'notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' and 'alert 48' on kafka all returned total_matched 0, returned 0, truncated false, first_match null (data_range 2026-04-02T08:00:00Z-2026-04-02T13:59:00Z, so the window is fully covered).

auth-service, order-service, portfolio-service and pricing-engine each returned total_matched 0 for the term 'certificate' (WARN+) over 12:10-13:00Z on 2026-04-02, with truncated false and first_match null; their data_range is 2026-04-02T08:00:00Z-13:59:00Z so the queried window is inside available data.

Combining this round with the previously cleared services, 8 of the non-payment components now show 0 in-window hits for cert/TLS-alert terms: kafka (4 patterns), auth-service, order-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine, plus api-gateway, settlement-service and ledger-db from the earlier round -- while payment-service itself is the only component with matches (134 TLS-related ERRORs from 12:15:27Z).

No matching record exists to quote verbatim from any swept service: every kafka and service result in this round has an empty entries array ("top_patterns":[],"entries":[]), so apart from payment-service no other service produced a cert-expiry log line in 12:10-13:00Z.

No record anywhere in change metadata references a certificate, CN, notAfter or rotation: across ALL services over 2026-03-01→2026-04-02T13:59Z, get_config_changes returns exactly one record, cfg-2502 (payment-service, key 'bank.api.timeout_ms', 3000→5000, 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z) — nothing referencing 'payments-client.orangeinvest.internal' or any 'orangeinvest.internal' cert identity.

No deployment in the whole 2026-03-01→2026-04-02T13:59Z period is cert-related: get_deployments (all services) returns a single entry, dep-5510, settlement-service v1.9.0 'new CSV exporter' at 2026-04-02T10:30:00Z, rolled_back_at null — no cert/CA/credential deploy exists to form a renewal batch.

The external peer bank-partner-api is entirely outside the change-record system: config-change and deployment queries scoped to bank-partner-api return count 0 for 2026-03-01→2026-04-02T13:59Z, so no bank-side TLS/CA reconfiguration record can be observed (supports H2 being unverifiable from records, not that H2 is false).

The dependency record exposes no certificate/secret node: bank-partner-api resolves as type 'external', owner 'vendor', has_telemetry=false with ZERO edges and itself as the only node, and payment-service's graph is only api-gateway (http), ledger-db (db), bank-partner-api (external), kafka (queue-produce) — no cert-manager/vault/keystore, so the client cert identity is not represented as a managed component.

Historical-incident search on the cert identity terms yields no record naming this CN or a fleet/CA renewal batch: querying 'client certificate expired renewal batch CA rotation orangeinvest.internal' returns only HIST-106 (2025-06-30, settlement-service, 'Client certificate expired; no renewal automation', category credential_expiry, match_score 4) and HIST-108 (JWT key rotation, match_score 1); a second query for 'payments-client.orangeinvest.internal mTLS client cert CN' returns only HIST-106 again (match_score 2). At most 2 historical records match, i.e. no prior orangeinvest.internal fleet-batch event is recorded.

Interpretation: on the record side the 12:15:00Z expiry looks ISOLATED to a single client identity (the bank-rail client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) rather than part of a wider fleet/CA renewal batch — the single cert-adjacent historical precedent (HIST-106) is a different service (settlement-service) almost a year earlier, and there is no rotation event, no fleet-wide deploy and no CA record in the 2026-03-01→13:59Z change history. This rests on absence of records in a toolset that also exposes no cert inventory (F19-F22), and is a lead, not proof.
